only three transits with near-gap p_chance 0.01181 - additional transits improve false-alarm test but current depths are consistent
dossier.public_summary: A shallow 0.6% flat-bottomed dip repeats every 13.1 days with no odd-even or secondary eclipse and a duration that matches a small M-dwarf host, and its size is about 3.7 Earth radii with no nearby star able to mimic it. The three detected transits are consistent in depth and the star-density fit is consistent with a planet, so a planet is the best explanation.

reasons.why: stellar density derived from transit matches stellar models (TIC and Gaia FLAME/GSP-Phot both give duration_ratio 1.09-1.23), supporting planet over diluted stellar companion
no star within one TESS pixel could cause the 6080 ppm dip with <=25% eclipse (closest that could is 25.9 arcsec away needing 0.2102 eclipse), and contratio 0.0162 is typical for single star
strongly flat-bottomed box-shaped dip favours planet over V-shaped grazing/eclipsing binary
odd_even depths consistent (diff_sigma 0.7645, ratio 1.1) and no secondary (snr 2.527 below 5, snr_at_half 0.04042) against EB at 2x period
undiluted depth 6178 ppm on 0.428 Rsun host gives planet size, below giant-planet limit, even with Gaia radii

three transits give consistent depths (chi2 5.326 dof 2, share_of_top_3 1.0, refit snr 11.29) and sectors p_constant 0.1501 (chi2 2.071 dof 1, depth change 26.29%) shows no sector-persistent change, inconsistent with blended binary
centroid was inconclusive with low SNR (11.15) and thus does not provide counter-evidence, and low xgboost planet_rank 0.07 is outweighed by flat bottom and density match
reasons.value: inconclusive (no sector with clear difference image) + centroid_all not_run
